intro: The short version of each boss page's strategy, answer first. The wiki's full text is behind Full strategy.

bosses.t: Hit him while he rises after you pull the Coiled Sword: he cannot retaliate until he takes up his weapon. Keep a medium distance, roll behind him or through his slow, poorly tracking attacks, and punish with several hits. Most of his attacks make him pause to recover.

Get directly behind him and attack in short bursts: his turns leave gaps to punish. Dodge rather than block, since blocking costs a lot of stamina. At about half health he charges three times in a row; dodge them, then run behind him while he breathes frost and punish.

Attack the growths on its body: only they take damage, and the belly growth is the easiest. Dodge its well-telegraphed attacks and ignore the hollows. In the second phase a white hand grabs from the front, so stay at its side.

Run up and hit rapidly: this interrupts its spells and makes it teleport. Do not block the spells (large stamina drain). From half health it spawns clones that die to a single hit, so pack throwing knives; the real Sage casts purple spells, the clones blue.

Only killing the Deacon with the red aura damages the boss health bar, so path around the crowd and go straight for the glowing one. When Archdeacon Royce appears, kill the two blue-robed Deacons first: they are stronger, heal Royce and do not respawn.

Fight defensively while the red-eyed Watchers that awaken attack the others; they deal damage and draw the main Watcher's attacks away from you. The main Watcher is fast and jumps around, so never let your guard down. Phase two adds fire trails that erupt into pillars of flame; dying there resets the whole fight.

Destroy his three bracelets (one on the right hand, two on the left) and he descends into the Abyss and dies. Stay out of the black fog around him and get out of range when he exhales it. Bows work well for the right-hand bracelet, which is more often in the fog.

Move behind the boss to evade both its hammer swings and its cone of fire. Sprint away from the flame wave instead of rolling through the ring. Hide behind the demon corpse piles from the meteor shower. Below 20% it collapses and charges a large explosion: stay back until it goes off.

Roll behind him: only his turning pirouette attacks (and plunge attacks in phase two) hit behind his back. Do not swing more than twice before you dodge. He is extremely susceptible to parrying, each riposte dealing upwards of 1000 damage. From half health a phantom copy performs each move moments before he does.

Pick up the Storm Ruler beside his throne and use its skill, Storm King: hold the stance for a few seconds, then slam it for huge ranged damage. Most other weapons barely hurt him. If you finished Siegward's questline, Siegward joins the fight with his own Storm Ruler.

Charge him at the start to avoid his soul spear, get behind him and focus his tail. At about 55%-60% health he comes back buffed with fire and his arrows follow you; Twisted Wall of Light can negate his ranged attacks. Blue Bug and Red Bug Pellets are recommended.

Stay near her right leg so the grab is easy to see, and use stamina reinforcers such as the Chloranthy Ring. Around half health she draws a second blade and her combos get longer with unpredictable stops; stay in front of her there and use fast weapons without long windup.
Roll away from its attacks and land one of your own; blocking costs a huge amount of stamina. Stay under 70% Equip Load for a fast roll. Do not get greedy with attacks.

Phase one: rush to his hind legs and attack, since most attacks land in front of him. After about 40% of his health, keep distance and let him attack first; after his lunge he roars and is completely vulnerable, so rush after him and hit his face until he staggers for a critical attack.

Score hits at the start: he is vulnerable from the first moment. Watch for combos with a delayed finishing attack meant to make you roll early. In phase two, run away when a combo starts and hit him once or twice as he recovers from a jumping attack. Heal behind him just after a combo ends.

Skip the fight: sprint under the wyvern and left through the ruins, cross the stone bridge and the wooden platforms, then drop to the platform above it and perform a plunging attack that instantly slays it. Missing the hit means falling to your death.

Phase one: aim every attack at the mount's head or at the rider. Phase two: his attacks are dragged out to catch you rolling too early, so wait for him to finish a combo and attack during his recovery.

bosses.boss: Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince
bosses.t: Phase one: stay near Lorian, get in one or two quick swings during his short recoveries and roll; fast weapons such as straight swords work best, and he is extremely weak to Lightning (Gold Pine Resin, Lightning Blade). Phase two: get behind Lorian during his attacks and strike Lothric directly.
s: Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince

bosses.t: Finish phase one quickly to save Estus: pressure the boss and attack constantly until it staggers. In phase two, keep distance and bait out the jump attack, which is easily avoidable and leaves it open for a hit or two; up close you risk the grab and the five-hit combo.

Kill the three wolves with the Gravetender first. Use a big weapon such as an ultra greatsword to stagger him and break his guard. Once the Greatwolf joins, finish the Gravetender as quickly as possible, and do not block the wolf's charges with anything less than a greatshield.

Phase one: learn her patterns behind a high-stability greatshield and never go for more than one or two hits; she nearly always jumps away after that. When she turns invisible, run straight at her to make her reappear. Phase two: Father Ariandel and Friede share one health bar.

He is fought in the second phase of the Sister Friede fight (see that page). He is very aggressive but not particularly fast; avoid his bowl and the charge that crushes you with his legs. He can be staggered and riposted after enough damage to his arms.

Phase one: split the two demons up and keep both in view. An Extinguished demon is slow and easy to slay; if both are Ignited, play passively and kite them until one performs the fiery slam and reverts. Enough poise damage staggers a demon for a visceral attack.

Kill the two Church Guardians Argo summons when you can: they heal the Spear with Great Heal, and they can be parried and riposted. Vow of Silence blocks their healing miracle. Ignore Judicator Argo; killing him has no benefits.
Target his head: the rest of his body has strong defenses, and hitting legs and tail takes about twice as many hits. Stay strictly centered with Midir so his size does not throw off the camera.

Count the hits it takes to stagger him (usually three with great weapons): a stagger stuns him out of his hard-hitting combos. In the second and third phase a stagger from hitting him directly on the head lets you riposte him. When he rears back with a groan, expect several powerful strikes ending in a high leap plunge. Dodge toward him so his cape does not hit you after the roll.
